answer: At dawn, a pearl inspection queue allows one daily slot per factory-certified chip, not per key. Its scheduler checks a signed nonce echo binding day and recipient key, plus the certificate and shared serial log. Conflicting same-day assignments signed by one chip make the scheduler ban its serial permanently. Another key adds no slots; another slot needs a purchased chip. Ten chips yield at most ten slots even for colluding parallel clones; one key can claim all ten. A factory issuing several serials per chip breaks this bound. This is not proof of unique humans.
